# Open-Derivations Ledger

*Authoritative list of everything in the model that is NOT yet derived from first principles — every quantity still fit, tuned, assumed, posited, phenomenological, or flagged "open". Regenerated by the Master Audit Prompt in `docs/roadmaps/open-derivations-prompts.md`.*

*Last audit: 2026-08-11 - 17:16. Sources swept: `docs/status/exactness-inventory.md` ("Currently failing / not-yet-met" + the Tier-3 rows for tuned/fit/anchor/calibration/scheme/residual), `findings-index.md` (keyword grep, full range, with F280–F309 read in full), the flagged `findings/F{N}-*.md` open/remaining sections following `[[links]]`, `docs/roadmaps/next-steps.md` + `next-steps-pt2.md`, `docs/status/completeness-2026-08-07.md` **including its two amendments**, and `tail -400 docs/status/changelog.md`. Frontier at this audit: **F309** is the newest finding (2026-08-11 - 16:55); **F314** remains the highest number (backlog numbers below the max are being drained on purpose — see CLAUDE.md §Concurrency). Prior audit ran 2026-08-05 and reached F314.*

**How to read this.** Part A = **targets** (a number or claim not yet derived). Part B = **closed-negative results** (a proven free parameter, an exact no-go, a settled null) — do not re-attack these as open. Part C = **closed-by-decision** founding posits. Part D is **new to this ledger**: a **contradiction** — two adopted results that disagree, which is neither a target, a no-go nor a posit, and which `completeness-2026-08-07` §"ledger observation" specifically recorded this file as having no row shape for. It has one now.

**Two scope corrections this audit makes, and they change the headline count.**

1. **The SM parameter block was never on this ledger.** The previous audit reported "genuinely-distinct open targets: 5" while the project's own parameter ledger (`completeness-2026-08-07` §D) read **14 of 28 open or absent**. Those 14 — six quark masses, four CKM entries, $\alpha_\text{em}$, $m_H$, $M_R$, the $\nu$ CP phase — are exactly what this file exists to list. They are now rows **E6–E9** and **D4**, mostly `scope` rather than `attacked`, which is a different and more honest statement than not appearing.
2. **A branch is not a residual.** Seven rubric rows and three ledger rows now hang off one unchosen rational number (Part D). Reporting $d_1$ as "one number, 36.2% open" without saying which *branch* it is being computed on understates it by six decades.

Where a row corresponds to a rubric row of `docs/status/completeness-2026-08-07.md`, that row is named so the two ledgers can be read against each other.

and does not reopen $p=2$ (F196) or CL275 (F311/F319's uniform-$\lambda$ exclusion — unaffected,
since sequestering is not that class of mechanism).

**Net effect on the grade: G1/K9 stays OPEN, but the residual has moved.** Before F367, no
dynamical mechanism of the required *type* had been checked against this model's numbers at all
(Weinberg's 1989 no-go theorem restricts any viable route to the non-local/global class F332 §5
identified but did not build). Now one has, and it structurally works for the reason required —
the OPEN → PARTIAL bar is not cleared because the mechanism is not adopted into the model's gravity
sector, and adoption is a decision-level question this finding deliberately leaves open rather than
answers. This is the **third** channel type checked for this row (after K2's $AB\equiv1$
sequestering and K3/K4's literal block-spin reading, both excluded) and the **first** to
structurally succeed rather than fail — a materially different outcome from F332's two closures,
recorded as such rather than folded into "another closed channel." **The sole route actually
inside the model remains F193 §B/F196/F241's capacity ceiling**, still undynamicised, still "the
number, no dynamics" — F367 supplies a well-matched *candidate* dynamics for the bare-sum side of
the problem, at a stated import cost, not a dynamics for that ceiling route itself. Also updated to
carry this forward: rubric **K9**, parameter **#28**, rubric **A11**, the module registry
(`_SPINE`, `interactions.cosmology_lambda_sequestering`), `tests/registry/interactions.yaml`
(`F367-cc-sequestering`, two verified controls), and `docs/claims/CL303-sequestering-selectivity-identity-not-adopted.md`
(`status: contingent`). **No leg, control, status, or value changed in any prior finding or
card**; F367 is additive.

**Addendum, 2026-09-05 - 02:50 — F367/CL303's own falsifier 4 run against the actual Kaloper-Padilla base action: PPN/F178-vacuum/induced-$G$ not in tension (CL303 stays contingent), two new adoption costs surfaced (F368).**
F367 named, and explicitly did not attempt, its own falsifier 4: *"a worked construction showing
sequestering's global Lagrange-multiplier sector is inconsistent with the model's other decision-4
content (PPN, the F178 vacuum-scope restriction, the induced-$G$ derivation) would close the
adoption question in the negative."* F368 (`findings/F368-cc-sequestering-consistency.md`, verdict
CONFIRMED-NARROWER after the mandated attack-and-fix pass) runs it, against Padilla's review sec.7
directly rather than F367's abridged local-consequence citation.

**Falsifier 4 does not fire.** In vacuum, Padilla's own local field equation reduces algebraically
(sympy-verified) to ordinary GR plus a $\Lambda_\text{eff}$ term — the Kottler/Schwarzschild-de
Sitter form, the same qualitative object this model's decision 4 already needs to explain — with
PPN corrections from a small $\Lambda$ utterly negligible at solar-system scales (standard, cited)
and the induced-$G$ coefficient untouched by construction (F367 S1, reused). **CL303's `status`
stays `contingent`, not `withdrawn`.**

**Two costs neither F367 nor CL303 had named are surfaced.** Padilla sec.7's *base* mechanism
(not only its "why now" scalar-potential extension) additionally requires (i) spatial closure
($k>0$), from the mechanism's own finite-total-4-volume requirement — independently
sympy-verified here that eternal de Sitter and ordinary flat/open matter-only expansion both give
divergent 4-volume while a closed matter-dominated recollapse gives finite 4-volume, matching what
the multiplier field needs; and (ii) non-eternal ("transient") dark energy, for the same
finite-volume reason. **Neither is excluded by current data.** Planck CMB-alone has a live,
*disputed* $>99\%$ C.L. preference for positive curvature (Di Valentino, Melchiorri & Silk 2020;
countered by Efstathiou & Gratton 2020 as a prior-volume artefact; resolved to flat once BAO is
added) — not claimed as evidence, only noted as a curious, contested alignment. DESI DR2's own
$w_0>-1,w_a<0$ preference ($3.1\sigma$ over $\Lambda$CDM with CMB) gives $dw/da>0$ — $w$ trending
less negative toward the future, the qualitative direction transience needs — reported as *not
contradicted, directionally aligned*, explicitly not as a derived prediction and **not as a
promotion or absorption of rubric K10**, which this does not touch (Amendment 4's instruction that
K10 must not yet absorb any K9 candidate mechanism stands unchanged).

**Net effect on the grade: G1/K9 stays OPEN; the adoption ledger is more complete, not shorter.**
The most direct route to closing off adoption (an inconsistency in the three legs falsifier 4
named) has now been checked and does not succeed — but two further, previously-invisible costs are
now on the record, both currently unexcluded by data. This narrows what "adopting sequestering"
would actually commit the model to, without changing whether it is adopted (still not) or whether
K9's grade moves (still OPEN). Also updated to carry this forward: rubric **K9**, parameter
**#28**, the module registry (`_SPINE`, `interactions.cosmology_lambda_sequestering_consistency`),
`tests/registry/interactions.yaml` (`F368-cc-sequestering-consistency`, three verified controls),
and `docs/claims/CL303-sequestering-selectivity-identity-not-adopted.md` (`status: contingent`,
unchanged; falsifier 4 marked checked-and-not-met; two new costs added to its body). **No leg,
control, status, or value changed in any prior finding or card**; F368 is additive.
